examples.text: Diese Beleidigung will er nicht auf sich sitzen lassen: Adolf Hitler tobt gerade in der Hölle angesichts der Behauptung Alice Weidels, er sei ein Kommunist gewesen. (...) examples.translation: Il ne veut pas se laisser insulter : Adolf Hitler est en train de se déchaîner en enfer face à l’affirmation d'Alice Weidel selon laquelle il était communiste. glosses: The infliction of severe pain or anguish, especially as an interrogation technique or punishment; (usually in the plural) a technique, method, or device which is designed to inflict such anguish.

examples.text: Using large dogs to attack bound, hand-cuffed prisoners is clearly torture.
What new tortures await me?
People confess to anything under torture.

If Cheney calls it enhanced interrogation, he argues, this still doesn’t change the meaning of the word torture, which Cheney and the public know perfectly well. But cognitive linguists like Lakoff (1996) remind us that the public can be manipulated into believing that torture is “merely” an enhanced interrogation technique and thus does not protest.

Santorum, in a comment regarding Senator John McCain's repudiation of torture, stated, "He doesn't understand how enhanced interrogation works. I mean, you break somebody, and after they've broken they become cooperative" (Summers 2011).

glosses: Severe pain or anguish, of mind or body.
An unpleasant sensation or its infliction: embarrassment, heartache, etc.

examples.text: Every time she says 'goodbye' it is torture!

glosses: To intentionally inflict severe pain or suffering on (someone), usually with the aim of forcing confessions or punishing them.
